recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中一顆中型母細胞，核質比高、染色質細緻，細胞質少、偏嗜鹼性並可見少量細小嗜天青顆粒，未見 Auer rod；背景紅血球有輕度大小不均與少數橢圓形紅血球。
features: Single medium-sized circulating blast, about twice the diameter of a red cell
High N:C ratio with a thin rim of basophilic cytoplasm
Round nucleus with finely granular chromatin; nucleoli not clearly resolved
Few fine azurophilic cytoplasmic/overlying granules; no Auer rods
Red cells with mild anisocytosis and occasional elliptocytes; no platelets clearly seen in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a medium-sized circulating blast with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, a round nucleus with finely granular chromatin and a scant rim of basophilic cytoplasm containing a few fine azurophilic granules. No Auer rods are identified. The background red cells show mild anisocytosis with occasional elliptocytes, and no leukocytes or platelets are evident in this field. Circulating blasts with azurophilic granules are consistent with peripheral involvement by acute myeloid leukemia; in this case, t(9;11)(p22;q23) supports AML with KMT2A-MLLT3.

ddx.vs: Lymphoblasts are typically agranular, so azurophilic granules favor myeloid lineage, but flow cytometry is needed for confirmation.
LGLs have abundant pale cytoplasm with coarse azurophilic granules and condensed mature chromatin, unlike this high N:C blast.
Promyelocytes have more abundant cytoplasm with numerous coarse primary granules and a perinuclear hof.
